blocks.text: Needs Work Dunhuang is a county-level city in northwestern Gansu Province, Western China. Historically known as Sachu (沙州), it was a major stop on the ancient Silk Road. It became especially significant as Buddhism spread along the Silk Road, leading to the construction and expansion of the nearby Mogao Caves, a complex of over 700 Buddhist grottoes carved into the cliffs, filled with Buddhist murals, sculptures, and manuscripts. Established as early as the 4th century CE, the Mogao Caves became a major center for Buddhist worship and artistic production.

In the 20th century, scholars and artists drew on the Mogao murals to inspire traditional dance. The style also influenced animation in the 1980s, when pioneering studios such as the Shanghai Animation Film Studio adapting stories from Dunhuang murals. In recent decades, Dunhuang Feng has developed into a mature, recognized design style that extends across video games, graphic design, and digital art.
The Dunhuang Feng is used in three interconnected branches: Historical, Design Aesthetics, and Performance Art.

Dunhuang Grottoes boast a distinctive visual style marked by vivid saturated mineral colors, fluid graceful linework, and a natural blend of Western Regions and traditional Chinese aesthetic temperaments. Its core iconic elements include ethereal Feitian (飞天) flying apsaras with fluttering long ribbons, elaborate lotus-themed zaojing (藻井) ceiling decorations, mild-featured painted Buddha and Bodhisattva statues, and spacious layered landscape & narrative mural compositions. Dynamic contours, soft color transitions and dense yet orderly decorative patterns make its artistic vibe elegant, unrestrained and recognizable.

Under Construction Dunhuang dance restores and reinterprets the music and dance postures from grotto murals—most notably the iconic S-shaped body rhythm and the classic "pipa playing behind the back" movement, popularized by the milestone dance drama Flower Rain on the Silk Road. It also encompasses contemporary innovative forms including immersive theater, digital light and shadow shows, cross-border modern dance, and virtual digital human performances.

Under Construction Influenced by the Guochao trend, Dunhuang Feng as a design aesthetics turns the visual elements from Dunhuang’s historical relics into an easy-to-copy, flexible design system for today’s creative design scene. The modern design favours warm colors. Desert frontier landscapes and oasis cities are also considered motifs of the design.

Some Dunhuang Feng designs featured in films and TV dramas, video games, dance performance costumes, ethnic-style portrait photography, wedding attire and other fields have been criticized as "entirely controlled by amateurs who never bother to conduct serious research. They have no intention of promoting traditional culture at all, and only aim to make money. As a result, they casually patch together [Dunhuang, Arabian and Indian] cultural elements purely based on their own imagination, with total disregard for cultural appropriation and the dignity of ethnic traditional culture."
